title: Building a cheap home NAS from used enterprise gear

title: UK motorists' taxes versus road spending

title: Analogy arguing diet books are fallacious

title: Brainstormed startup ideas for others
why: A list of unvetted product ideas with no analysis; an invitation to collaborate rather than lasting insight.

title: git reset --hard can destroy uncommitted work
why: Changes never committed never enter the object database, so reflog cannot recover them after git reset --hard; commit or stash first.

title: Why cabinet makers cut quality for mass market
why: Most buyers can't judge construction, so premium materials earn no price premium; veneers and laminates win the middle market.

title: Simulators train real-car reflexes that transfer
why: Steering and throttle corrections drilled in a sim become subconscious habits, and a racer reports they carried into a real crash recovery.

title: Personal account of chelation treatment
why: Anecdotal medical claims about chelation and tinnitus; not reliable evidence and no generalizable lesson for readers.

title: Argument about piracy and estimated losses
why: Legal and economic argument about copyright loss estimates; opinion-driven debate rather than explanation.

title: How futures exchanges began as hedging tools
why: Standardized contracts and clearinghouses let farmers hedge price risk, with speculators taking the other side; complex derivatives grew out of this.

title: Rebuttal that startup success can be designed

title: Why algebra was a hard-won abstraction

title: Personal account of rising from poverty

title: Personal story of a low-paid startup job

title: Founder transition from implementer to leader
why: Personal career advice about giving up day-to-day implementation; experience-based but not a technical explanation.

title: Meeting 30 colleagues in week one

title: Observations on m68k TLS syscall overhead

title: Why the early web is remembered too fondly
why: Opinion on nostalgia and aging; the observation is plausible but not supported by technical or factual detail.

title: Estimating crypto share of GPU sales
why: Speculative estimate of mining demand in Nvidia and AMD revenue, based on pricing inference rather than disclosed figures.

title: Derivatives as linear approximations, not functions
why: Treat the derivative as the tangent-line linear map at a point; this view makes forward and reverse-mode autodiff intuitive.

title: Critique of Matrix clients and Element branding
why: Product and business complaints about Element's clients and sales; opinion about a project rather than technical explanation.

title: Depression as illness versus weakness
why: Personal and social argument about depression and attrition-based workplaces; sincere but opinion-based.

title: Response to an article on harassment
why: Commentary on a community dispute and how to read an article; contextual argument not meaningful on its own.

title: Safari experience and meat-eating ethics
why: Personal travel anecdote and ethical argument about hunting and meat; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Searle: computation is observer-relative, not intrinsic
why: Computation is defined by interpreting physical states as symbols, so a program alone doesn't guarantee mind; physical causal powers matter.

title: Argument that ML is just curve fitting
why: Dismissive opinion that ML is applied math and hype; promotes classical methods without a specific, checkable comparison.

title: Why capital mobility breaks comparative advantage
why: Ricardo assumed fixed labor and capital; when capital flows to cheap labor, employment shifts across countries rather than staying stable.

title: Business analysis of Spotify buying Echo Nest
why: Opinion on acquisition finance, IPO motives and label deals; speculative business commentary.

title: Personal career and contracting history
why: Autobiographical account of contracting and income; sincere but no transferable technical lesson.

title: Employer view of a candidate's website
why: Hiring critique tied to a dispute about sexism; argumentative, with little general guidance beyond opinion.

title: CUDA threads, blocks, grids and kernels explained
why: Blocks cannot communicate across SMs and kernel launches are costly; massive threading hides memory latency, so favor large problems and low memory use.

title: First-hand account of Harvey boat volunteers
why: Account of volunteer boats and app coordination; interesting but mostly anecdotal and not a generalizable technical lesson.

title: Position on end-to-end encryption and EARN IT
why: Policy and personal-responsibility argument about encryption laws; opinion and self-presentation rather than explanation.

title: Why Microsoft focuses on productivity and enterprise
why: Opinion on company strategy and Office's strengths; subjective business commentary without verifiable detail.

title: Reputation replaces age as trust proxy
why: Plausible argument that reputation systems replace institutional age as trust signals; opinion-level, not substantiated.

title: Semantic web's later evolution beyond RDF/XML
why: The article skipped Turtle, JSON-LD, SPARQL and linked-data work; the semantic web's later history is more substantial than RDF/XML suggests.

title: Navigate a large .emacs with outline headers
why: Use ;;;; section headers with occur and a regex to show an outline; set quiet startup with inhibit-startup-message and a custom echo message.

title: Lowering barriers for non-English open-source contributors
why: Japanese contributors often underrated their English; x264 grew Japanese patch flow by making language and mailing-list intimidation less of a barrier.

title: Critique of Coursera's MOOC-about-MOOCs course
why: Argues a MOOC course on MOOCs was poorly vetted and that the field is in flux; opinion about one course's management.

title: Defense of bash as an interactive REPL
why: Argument for shell scripting as a quick REPL; general opinion with caveats about process merging but no concrete technique.

title: Rent-seeking argument about app platforms
why: Economic argument that platform gatekeeping is rent seeking; interesting framing but mostly opinion without concrete evidence.

title: Type-safe C arrays via macros on plain variables
why: Represent an array as data, length and capacity variables generated by macros; this avoids casts and keeps debugger views readable.

title: Why tech acquisitions often go badly

why: Most chip designs integrate licensed ARM and interface cores like Lego, specifying connections in block diagrams or GUI tools.

why: Stack allocation is fast because locals and return addresses follow call order; heap allocation suits data that must outlive the function call.

title: Skeptical take on 2014 Bitcoin predictions

title: Questions about MVC versus code-behind

title: Why GR alternatives face strict astrophysical limits
why: GR's field equations hold everywhere except near the big bang, inside black holes and in quantum superpositions, so alternatives must match GR in ordinary regimes.

title: Per-TTY task groups cut desktop latency under load
why: Mike Galbraith's small scheduler patch groups tasks per TTY; his tests showed average desktop latency dropping about 60x under heavy CPU load.

title: Personal story of a tough US school
why: Autobiographical account of school, fights and loans; personal rather than instructive.

title: Why TPMs make poor DRM foundations
why: TPM keys attest boot-stage combinations, so a BIOS update breaks DRM tied to it, unlike hardware-bound keys; SGX and SEV serve isolation instead.

title: Frustration with Drupal module maintenance
why: Experience-based complaint about unresponsive maintainers and contributed modules; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Sandberg's farewell letter to Meta
why: Personal farewell reflection on joining and leaving Facebook; no technical or transferable lesson.

why: Political-economic opinion about the CCP and economic opening; contested generalization without evidence.

title: Top-10 words idioms compared across languages

title: Critique of Perl for large projects

title: Critique of a roguelike's landing page
why: Product usability critique about choice overload on a game website; opinion-driven feedback.

title: Marine veteran on the forever war
why: Personal military experience and political reflection; sincere but not a technical or instructive lesson.

why: A symlinked .forward pointed at /etc/shadow let root-run sendmail dump the password file to port 25 for offline cracking.

title: Why meme posts degrade HN threads
why: Opinion on memes and upvoting culture in community; subjective with no technical substance.

title: Objection to rustfmt column alignment

why: Break the question into population, haircut frequency and cancelling assumptions to reach an order-of-magnitude answer; the method matters more than the number.

title: Lessons from clients who stopped paying

why: Argumentative rebuttal of an article on Antarctic sea ice and models; contains some physics but mostly rhetorical dispute.

title: Why the dipole drive can't beat energy conservation
why: Ion clouds form outside the plates and cancel the net electric force, so the device can't keep accelerating; the energy must come from somewhere.
